articles.title: Ujjain Hanuman Temple Row: 170-Year-Old Idol Stays Put as Devotees Oppose Removal for Road Widening
articles.description: A unique dispute over a 170-year-old Hanuman idol has emerged in Ujjain, where the district administration is facing strong resistance from devotees over plans to relocate the religious structure for road widening. The temple, popularly known as Khade Hanuman Mandir because of the standing idol, has become the centre of attention as preparations for the 2028 Simhastha continue across the religious city. Several religious structures in the area have reportedly already been removed as part of the widening work, but authorities have struggled to shift the Hanuman idol despite repeated efforts. News of the administration’s attempts has spread widely through Instagram and other social media platforms, prompting devotees from different parts of the country to visit the temple and offer prayers. Devotees argue that the idol, which has remained at the location for around 170 years, should not be moved and that authorities should find an alternative solution for the road expansion. Many visitors have expressed deep emotional attachment to the temple and said the existing road arrangement does not significantly obstruct movement. Some devotees have also questioned why the temple cannot remain at its original location while development work continues around it. The issue has now turned into a sensitive matter involving faith, heritage and urban development, with devotees firmly demanding that the idol remain where it has stood for generations. As Ujjain prepares for the massive influx of pilgrims expected during Simhastha 2028, the administration faces the challenge of balancing infrastructure development with religious sentiments and public faith.

articles.title: Iran to join Saudi-Pak-Turkey ‘Islamic NATO’? Russia backs Tehran's entry into Mecca defence pact
articles.description: Russia is reportedly backing Iran’s possible entry into a Saudi-Pakistan-Turkey security arrangement, raising questions about the emergence of a new regional defence bloc. The proposed framework, described as an “Islamic NATO” by some commentators, could bring Iran closer to Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey despite longstanding rivalries. Moscow’s reported support for Tehran’s participation adds another layer to the shifting Middle East power balance. If Iran joins the emerging Mecca Defence Pact, the move could reshape security cooperation across the Gulf and complicate calculations for Israel and the United States. Could this alliance mark a major new geopolitical shift?

articles.title: PM Modi Gujarat Visit: ₹35,000 Crore Projects, Youth Outreach and Major Development Push
articles.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to visit Gujarat today, where he will participate in several programmes in Vadodara and Navsari and inaugurate and lay the foundation stones for major development projects. During his visit to Vadodara, PM Modi will attend a programme at the University Ground, where development works worth more than ₹35,000 crore are expected to be inaugurated or launched. He will also address a public gathering and interact directly with beneficiaries and citizens. A large number of young people have reportedly registered online to attend the event, raising expectations that the Prime Minister may deliver a special message focused on youth, employment, education and development. Gujarat is gearing up to welcome PM Modi, with several major projects lined up during the visit. According to the details shared, central projects worth around ₹32,606 crore and state projects worth approximately ₹2,597 crore will be inaugurated or launched across Vadodara, Navsari and other parts of the state. The visit is also expected to give a major boost to railway infrastructure, with the foundation stone for the Vadodara-Ratlam rail track project among the key announcements. Other projects include a 110 MW floating solar power project and the inauguration of around 13,888 housing units. The Prime Minister’s Gujarat visit is being seen as a significant development push covering infrastructure, railways, renewable energy and housing. With thousands of people, particularly young attendees, expected to participate in the Vadodara programme, all eyes will be on PM Modi’s address and the announcements made during his Gujarat tour.

UP Politics: Samajwadi Party Student Wing Adopts Blue T-Shirts, Eyes Dalit Vote Ahead of 2027
articles.description: The Samajwadi Party has changed the dress code of its student wing, the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha, with the organisation set to replace its earlier maroon shirts and white trousers with blue T-shirts and jeans. The new T-shirts carry the message “Education, Creativity and Struggle” and are being launched by party chief Akhilesh Yadav at the Samajwadi Party office. Party leaders and student activists have described the change as part of a new political vision and outreach strategy aimed at connecting with students, youth and the PDA social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities. The blue colour is being projected by party workers as a symbol of peace, loyalty, knowledge and social change. The move also comes amid a broader visual shift within the Samajwadi Party, with Akhilesh Yadav increasingly seen using blue elements in his public appearances and press conference backgrounds. Party workers say the new colour scheme represents a “blue revolution” and an effort to strengthen grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Political observers are likely to view the move in the context of the party’s attempt to expand its appeal among Dalit voters and challenge the Bharatiya Janata Party’s political dominance in the state. The new student-wing uniform is therefore being presented not merely as a change in appearance, but as a political messaging exercise focused on youth mobilisation, social justice and the PDA narrative. The development has sparked discussion over the symbolism of colours in Uttar Pradesh politics and the Samajwadi Party’s electoral strategy for 2027.

articles.description: Ukraine is considering a controversial new source of wartime cash as its battle against Russia drains state finances. The proposal comes amid a bizarre contradiction: adult creators can face prosecution despite tax authorities pursuing their earnings. Nearly 7,900 Ukrainian creators reportedly made more than $131 million through OnlyFans in 2023. With another difficult winter of fighting looming, could Ukraine's booming underground adult-content economy become an unlikely source of funding for Zelensky's drone war?

articles.title: 'Shameful': Singapore Probes Anti-Indian Hate Wave, Racism With China Link Under Scanner
articles.description: Singapore is probing racist comments aimed at Indians after Nepal floods and an Air India funding row. Senior Minister K Shanmugam called the abuse shameful and unacceptable. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong warned that hate must not become normal. The comments used slurs and attacked Indian-origin executives linked to Air India. In June, Singapore blocked 14 anti-Indian posts. Its Home Affairs Ministry said they likely came from a China-based platform and sought to inflame racial tension. Why are Indians targeted? Is India facing a new information war? Can online hate damage Singapore’s model? This India-focused report examines racism, foreign influence, Air India, Singapore and the fight to stop hostile narratives from turning a business debate and a disaster into an attack on an entire community. It asks who amplifies the anger and who benefits from distrust.
